decisions.reason: As a low-cost complementary cleaning product tied to the installed base of the firm's wood floors, it remains a cheap option to keep open and there is still no strong negative signal warranting withdrawal.

The maintenance oil line fits the core flooring-aftercare system well, and for a growing, innovation-active firm the cost of continuing to learn about demand is likely modest relative to the cross-selling upside.
This care line for oiled floors is still worth retaining as a niche option, but its narrower use case and partial overlap with adjacent care products keep the pruning risk somewhat higher.
An underlay with moisture protection strengthens the firm's system offer around floor installation and is likely inexpensive to maintain while market evidence continues to accumulate.

The high-density underlay foam is still defensible to keep as part of a complete flooring solution, though its more commoditized character and possible overlap with other underlays make rationalization more plausible than for most other launches.

The oak parquet line is close to the firm's core capabilities and strategic direction, so despite higher carrying costs than accessories management would typically keep it on the market while refining which variants prove strongest.
